description_full: Independent Bank Corporation operates as the bank holding company for Independent Bank that provides banking services in the United States. The company offers demand deposits, interest checking, money market accounts, savings accounts, and time certificates of deposit, including free checking accounts. It also provides consumer loans that consists of real estate loans comprising residential mortgages and home equity loans and lines, all secured by one-to-four family residential properties, as well as other consumer loans; and investment and financial services. In addition, the company offers cash management; investment management and trust services; additional services, such as estate settlement, financial planning, tax services, and other special services; sale of mutual fund shares, unit investment trust shares, third party model portfolios, general securities, and fixed and variable annuities, as well as life insurance products; debit and credit card; safe deposit box services; automatic teller machines; and internet and mobile banking services. Independent Bank Corporation was founded in 1864 and is based in Grand Rapids, Michigan.

financial_summary: Independent Bank Corporation is a small-cap financial services business with a $802M market cap on $226M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +3.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 23% against a 8% cost of capital — a 14-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $70M in free cash flow — roughly 31 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.12× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield of 4.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 4.8% of the shares.

Piotroski score 4/9 — below the median for a healthy business

Late-cycle dynamics increase the probability of a slowdown
Credit cycles and regulatory capital — losses accumulate invisibly in good years and appear all at once, and the time to worry is when underwriting standards are loosest.
Fintech disintermediation — neobanks, embedded finance, and blockchain rails are unbundling the fee streams that traditional banks took for granted.
Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.02 across 512 companies in the universe; the top four hold 20% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 20% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 7% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 23% and a beta of 0.71, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.23 vs 5y 0.64), so read it loosely.
About $6.1M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 57% in the 2020 crash, 29% in the 2022 bear market and 93% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 54% below its DCF fair value of $79.55, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 31%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $62.87 to $104 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 41% above its 10-year median.
The 5 covering analysts target $41.20 on average, 13% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 7.0% annual cash-flow growth, 15pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 23% clears the cost of capital of 8.3% by 14pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.25).
It converts 31% of revenue into free cash flow.
It earns a 14% return on equity.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 2.2% over 3 years, 2.0% over 5 years and 7.0% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Analysts expect 17.9% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 4.8%, and institutions hold 84%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (17 sales, net $241K sold).
It returns 4.2% a year to shareholders (1.6% in buybacks and 3.1% in dividends).
The share count has grown 0.8% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years, raising it 4.2% a year over the last five.
people: With about 735 employees, each generates about $307K of revenue, 0.6x the Financial Services median, and productivity has risen 3.4% a year.
That works out to $95K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.1M (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
